newsitem.title: UK: BT backs MCI call for open markets.
newsitem.headline: BT backs MCI call for open markets.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc added its voice to that of its U.S. merger partner, MCI Communications Corp, calling for the effective opening up of the U.S. telecommunications market.

MCI, which issued a profit warning on Thursday, has said its attempts to break into local U.S. markets were being hampered by the "anti-competitive behaviour" from dominant local rivals, BT's chief executive Peter Bonfield called on regulators to ensure open markets.
"Effective competition needs regulators constantly to be vigilant and continually to introduce and enforce new measures as incumbents react to competition," Bonfield said in a statement.
"If consumers are to reap the full benefits of competition, there needs to be effective follow through by regulators to ensure open markets. It is what takes place in the markets that counts."

While Bonfield called for the same proactive approach to regulation to be adopted throughout the world, he said it was of particular importance in the U.S. "which so often provides the lead for others to follow".
MCI is America's second biggest long-distance telecoms operator. It said on Thursday it would forge ahead with the heavy investments it has been making to break into local telephone markets.
The group said local market losses for the year could reach $800 million, more than twice what it had originally planned. Losses in 1998 in its local business could exceed those in 1997, it added.
